The hypothalamus is a brain region crucial for regulating many bodily functions, including hormone release, body temperature, hunger, and sleep-wake cycles.
The hypothalamus is responsible for regulating the secretion of hormones, and the pituitary gland releases these hormones into the bloodstream.

Melatonin is a hormone secreted by the pineal gland in response to darkness, often called the "hormone of darkness".
It helps regulate the sleep-wake cycle by sensing light and dark through signals received from the retina of the eye.

The thyroid is a butterfly-shaped gland located in the neck.
It produces a hormone called thyroxine, which plays a vital role in increasing the body's metabolism.
The production of thyroxine requires iodine, a mineral obtained from our diet.
A deficiency of iodine can lead to hypothyroidism, a Liver condition where the body doesn't produce enough thyroid hormone.

This deficiency may also cause the thyroid gland to enlarge, leading to a condition known as goitre. An excess production of iodine can result in hyperthyroidism, where the thyroid becomes overactive and produces too much thyroxine.
Calcitonin- Helps in regulating calcium level in blood.
T3 (triiodothyronine) and T4 (thyroxine) are primary thyroid hormones regulating body metabolism, energy production, growth, and development.
The parathyroid glands are four small glands located behind the thyroid gland in the neck.
The main role of the parathyroid glands is to regulate the level of calcium in the blood and bones. They do this by producing a hormone called parathyroid hormone (PTH).
Diabetes Insipidus is caused when the body produces too much urine and is not able to retain water (due to lack of ADH/Vasopressin).
It is a cap-like structure located above both the kidneys.
It releases Adrenal hormone — also known as "Flight-or- Fight hormone".
It increases the blood pressure, heart rate, and metabolism in response to stress level.
Deficiency causes: Addison's disease (a rare chronic condition in which your adrenal glands don't produce enough of the hormones cortisol (stress hormone) and aldosterone).
Hormones:
Cortisol- Regulates metabolism, blood sugar levels and helps the body manage stress.
Aldosterone- Regulates blood pressure by controlling salt and water balance.
Androgens- Precursors for sex hormones that influence secondary sexual characteristics.
Epinephrine/Adrenaline & Norepinephrine/Noradrenaline- Responsible for the fight and flight response, increasing heart rate, blood pressure and energy levels during acute stress.

The liver is positioned in the upper right portion of the abdomen, beneath the diaphragm. It is a large organ.
The liver is responsible for numerous functions, including filtering blood, producing bile for digestion, metabolizing proteins, carbohydrates, and fats, and storing glycogen and vitamins.

A heterocrine gland is a gland that functions as both an endocrine gland and an exocrine gland.
Examples of heterocrine glands: Pancreas
Pancreas releases both hormones and enzymes (covered in digestive system) thus acting as a mixed gland.
It is the second largest gland of our body.
